location: PV-PORT sheets 02/04: K201/K401 coil (A_KM_COIL/B_KM_COIL), D201/D401, D202/D402, RV201/RV401, Q202/Q402; K202/K402 coil (A_KP_COIL), D203/D403, D204+D205/D404+D405
finding: Coil suppression is bypassed, so both the main contactor and the precharge relay open slowly. At de-energisation coil+ swings negative and the series feed diodes D201 (anode on the DO line) and D202 (anode on the hold switch) become FORWARD biased: the SYS-IO-AUX DO clamp (SMAJ12A+SMAJ36A, OUT -14.1..-15.7 V) and the avalanche of Q202 sit in parallel with RV201. The HVC43 coil therefore demagnetises at about -15..-16.5 V instead of through the S10K30 (V1mA 42-52 V); the varistor never conducts. The block note claim 'series diode keeps the varistor clamp away from the SYS driver' is wrong. Same on K202/K402: the 37.6-41.5 V zener path D204/D205 is bypassed by the ~16 V DO path through D203.
evidence: HVC43MC.pdf p7: 'if an alternative coil suppression device is used, the clamping voltage must not be smaller than 50 V'; p11: coil must be switched off instantly for a successful break; p3 break <=15 ms and the 450 A/1000 V cut-off are given for that drive. G7L-X.pdf p2 note *5 (release time and 1000 VDC durability measured with diode+zener), p5 'zener voltage 1 to 2 times the rated coil voltage' (24-48 V). Netlists: D201 K=A_KM_COIL A=K_A_MAIN; D202 K=A_KM_COIL A=A_HC_OUT; SYS-IO-AUX D903 SMAJ36A K=K_A_MAIN A=DO2_FW, D904 SMAJ12A K=GND A=DO2_FW. Calc: coil+ = -(13.3..14.7 + 0.8 + 0.85) = -15.0..-16.4 V; with L=2 H (A_L_COIL_K) initial di/dt (16+24)/2 = 20 A/s vs (60+24)/2 = 42 A/s with the varistor: release roughly 2-2.5x slower.
proposed_fix: Make the coil suppressor the lowest-voltage flyback path: e.g. drive the coils low-side (coil+ on the port-board 24 V, one >=100 V N-MOSFET from coil- to GND gated by the DO line and one gated by the hold logic, S10K30 directly across the coil) and re-check the dual-channel E-stop cut-off with that topology; or use reverse-blocking (back-to-back MOSFET) feeds rated >=100 V. For K202/K402 put diode+zener directly across the coil with the feed unable to source negative current.

location: PV-PORT sheets 02/04: Q202/Q402 (DMP4065S-7), D202/D402, nets A_HC_OUT/B_HC_OUT, +24V
finding: The hold switch is driven beyond its VDS rating on every contactor release. Through the forward-biased D202 its drain follows coil+ (about -15..-16.4 V, see PA-01) while its source is on +24V. If the SYS harness is unplugged or another DO stage is used, Q202 itself becomes the lowest clamp: it avalanches at about -45 V and absorbs roughly twice the coil energy in a SOT-23. If it fails short, the coil is fed from +24V permanently and the contactor can only be opened by removing all 24 V.
evidence: DMP4065S.pdf p2: VDSS -40 V, no avalanche (EAS/IAR) rating. Calc: VDS = coil+ + VF(D202) - V24 = -(16.4 - 0.5) - 26.4 = -42.2 V at the top of the 21.6-26.4 V window (-40.9 V with the lowest SMAJ12A VBR). Avalanche case: E_Q202 ~ E_L x VBR/(VBR - V24) ~ 2.1 x 0.5 x 2 H x 0.27^2 = 0.15 J.
proposed_fix: Use a >=100 V P-MOSFET with a gate-source zener for Q202/Q402 (and keep D202 >=100 V) together with the PA-01 topology change so that no feed switch ever acts as the coil clamp.

location: PV-PORT sheets 02/04: R220/R420 (RH100 1.5 k), Q203/Q403, Q204/Q404, U205/U405 (TPSI3050), K_DISCH line (J102 pin 5, shared by both ports)
finding: The fail-safe active discharge has no protection against being switched on while the port is connected to a live source. Any single loss of the hold-off chain during operation - K_DISCH wire/connector open, SYS DO5 off or failed, U205/U405 VDRV stuck low, Q204/Q404 open - puts R_dis across the running bus: 667 W at 1000 V (807 W at 1100 V) continuously in a 100 W chassis resistor, on both ports at once because K_DISCH is shared. Nothing on the board detects it (0.67 A extra port current). The same happens on every hardware-chain trip while the hold-closed interlock keeps a contactor closed (SYS cuts K_DISCH; the hold lasts until the fuse clears, up to ~200 s).
evidence: RH.pdf p3: RH100 = 100 W only on a 12x12x0.125 in Al panel at 25 C, 40 W free air; p4 derating -> ~84 W at 60 C; p1 continuous working voltage sqrt(P x R) = 387 V for 1.5 k; p5 overload only 5 x P for 5 s. Calc 1000^2/1500 = 667 W, 1100^2/1500 = 807 W = 6.7-8 x rating. gen/sys_io_aux.py sheet 09: 'K_DISCH (DO5) is held on only while both channels are healthy'; port_design report sec. 6.2 longest hold 197 s.
proposed_fix: Make the discharge thermally safe when it is triggered with the source connected: time-limit it (e.g. RC on the Q203 gate so it turns off after 5-10 s: <=6.7 kJ, absorbed by the RH100 mass) and/or add a thermal cut-off in the R_dis path, and/or block it while FB_x_MAIN = closed; let firmware verify the VA decay at every shutdown so a stuck-on discharge is detected.

location: PV-PORT sheets 02/04: hold-closed interlock U201-U204, Q201/Q202, D202, R203-R217 (and U401-U404, Q401/Q402, R403-R417)
finding: The hold-closed interlock is a single-channel protective function with no diagnostic coverage: neither the HOLD nor the OC state is read back by CTRL and there is no test injection. Many single faults leave it silently disabled. Disables the hold (undetectable): R203/R208 open; R205/R210 open (trip unreachable); R207/R212 open (trip moves to 548 A, above the 450 A cut-off); TLV3502, LVC1G32 or LVC1G11 output stuck low; Q201, Q202 or D202 open; R216 open; R217 short; R213 open; R215 short; IA_DIAG stuck low. Holds the contactor closed against any command (seen only afterwards as FB=closed; cleared only by removing +24V): Q201 or Q202 D-S short; comparator/OR/AND output stuck high; REF3030 output low (trips at ~0 A); R204/R209 open (39 A); R206/R211 open (114 A); DIAG stuck high with the AMC3302 in fail-safe (-2.57 V trips side B).
evidence: Recalculated from the netlist: +IN = 0.5 OUTP; -IN = 0.499 OUTN + 0.2807 VREF -> trips at Vdiff 1.683 V = 410 A (matches port_spec 410.5 A). Same network with single faults: R207 open 548 A, R206 open 114 A, R204 open 39 A, REF = 0 V trips at ~0 A, REF = 3.3 V 452 A, R205 open never (needs OUTP > 3.36 V; AMC3302 clips at +/-2.49 V, SBASA11B p7). J101 carries no HOLD/OC signal (interfaces.PORT).
proposed_fix: Add a proof test that firmware runs at every start: a CTRL- or SYS-driven input that moves the threshold to a few tens of amps (or injects an offset on +IN), plus readback of A_HC_HOLD/A_HC_OC on a spare DI or ADC; or duplicate the chain (2 channels with cross-check). Record the remaining latent faults in the ISO 13849 analysis that report sec. 6.2 already calls for.

location: PV-PORT sheets 02/04: R219/R419 (RH100 220R precharge), R220/R420 (RH100 1k5 discharge)
finding: The pulse capability of the RH100 resistors is not demonstrated. The design treats the datasheet overload test (5 x P for 5 s = 2.5 kJ) as an energy budget for pulses at 9x that power. Precharge peaks at 4.55 kW (45 x P), with 135-500 J per precharge, 757 J per faulted attempt and 2.27 kJ for 3 attempts. R_dis peaks at 667 W with up to 500 J. The RH datasheet gives no single-pulse or adiabatic rating. Its continuous working-voltage limit sqrt(P x R) is 148 V for 220 ohm and 387 V for 1.5 k, against the 1000-1100 V the resistors see.
evidence: RH.pdf p1 (max working voltage = (P x R)^1/2 or 1900 V, whichever is less), p5 (short time overload 5 x rated power for 5 s), no pulse curve. port_spec precharge E_worst_J 757; report sec. 1 'RH100 survives 0.55 s (5 x P for 5 s = 2500 J)' and the report's own open item 'no adiabatic pulse curve'. Calc 1000^2/220 = 4545 W.
proposed_fix: Obtain Vishay single-pulse energy data for RH100 220R and 1k5 at 4.5 kW / 0.1-1 s and 0.67 kW / 1-5 s, or use resistors with a published pulse-energy rating (ceramic bulk or a pulse-rated wirewound) sized for >= 757 J at 4.55 kW plus 3 attempts.

location: PV-PORT sheet 04: FV401 (DEHN 952515) on port B (B_F+/B_F-/PE)
finding: The port-B SPD is a PV-type arrester rated ISCPV 10 kA, but port B faces a battery or DC bus. The design assumes a 20 kA prospective short-circuit current there and allows up to 50 kA (L/R <= 1 ms). Neither the SPD's end-of-life short nor its SCI disconnector is rated for that source, and coordination with F401/F402 (160 A gPV) as backup protection is not confirmed.
evidence: sim/port_design.py: SPD_ISCPV = 10e3 (DEHN product page F31519; no PDF on file); report assumptions A_IPSC_BATT = 20 kA; report sec. 13 allows a battery prospective current <= 50 kA. ISCPV is defined for PV generator sources (IEC 61643-31).
proposed_fix: Use a DC SPD rated for battery/stiff DC sources with a short-circuit rating >= the port-B prospective current, or obtain DEHN's written coordination of 952515 with the HP10NH1GPV160 backup fuse at 20-50 kA, 1000 V DC.

location: PV-PORT sheets 02/04: C201/C401 (A_F+/A_F-) and C202/C402 (A_X+/A_X-), KEMET C4AQUBU4220A1YJ
finding: The X capacitors are not coordinated with the SPD let-through. C201 sits directly across the SPD, whose pole-pole protection level is Up <= 4 kV; C202 follows it through the choke's 1-3 uH leakage. A Type-2 surge therefore drives them to about 2.5-4 kV for tens of microseconds, against a surge rating of 1.5 x VNDC = 1950 V, allowed at most 10 times per lifetime. The X capacitors are missing from the report's sec. 9 coordination table.
evidence: C4AQ.pdf p5: surge voltage 1.5 x VNDC for maximum 10 times in a lifetime; test 1.5 x VNDC for 10 s; p7: 'the peak voltage shall not exceed the rated voltage VNDC' (1300 V at 70 C hot spot). port_spec spd Up_V 4000; report sec. 9 lists contactor, fuse bases, AMCs, TPSI, RH100, dividers, IMD and Y capacitors but not the X capacitors.
proposed_fix: Use X capacitors with a surge/impulse rating >= the SPD protection level (surge-rated PP film, 2-3 kV class), or add an SPD stage with a lower pole-pole Up ahead of them, and add the X capacitors (and AUX-HV, see AX-01) to the coordination table.

finding: The HV-to-PELV isolator packages are too small for the board's own insulation claim. The title block claims reinforced insulation for 1000 V DC working at PD2. At 1000 V, PD2, material group I, reinforced insulation needs 2 x 5.0 mm = 10 mm creepage, and the clearance for an 8 kV reinforced impulse is about 8 mm at <= 2000 m, x1.14 at 3000 m (PV-C6). The AMC parts offer >= 8 mm creepage/clearance and the TPSI3050 >= 8.5 mm. Unlike AUX-HV (CNY65B note), PV-PORT records no coating or potting requirement. U603 is not affected because its barrier sits between PE and GND.
evidence: AMC3330.pdf p6 and AMC3302.pdf p6 (insulation specifications): CLR >= 8 mm, CPG >= 8 mm, CTI >= 600; TPSI3050-Q1.pdf p6: CLR/CPG >= 8.5 mm; each datasheet: 'creepage and clearance requirements should be applied according to the specific equipment isolation standards'. PV-PORT comment1 'HV-PELV reinforced (1000 VDC working, OVC II, PD2 inside)'. IEC 60664-1 Table F.5 (indicative values, as used in sim/out/aux_hv_design/report.md sec. 11).
proposed_fix: Specify conformal coating to PD1 (IEC 60664-3) over the isolator footprints and record it as a board requirement, and confirm clearance at 3000 m with the SPD-controlled overvoltage under ECO-10; otherwise choose parts with >= 10 mm creepage.

location: PV-PORT sheet 06: Q601 (IMD P switch, source on PE, drain IMDP_SW), Q602 (IMD N switch), test strings R615-R622 / R627-R634
finding: The IMD test switches are single MOSFETs, so they do not block in reverse. Q601's body diode (VSD ~3.8 V) conducts whenever A_X+ is more than ~4 V below PE, connecting the 992 k test string to PE while the switch is 'open'. This is a normal state on PV-PORT: with a dark or low-voltage PV array and port B live, A_X+ ~ BUS- ~ -V_B/2 relative to PE (common negative). In that state the baseline and state-N readings are corrupted (R_iso reads low, giving nuisance alarms) and an unintended PE current of up to ~0.5 mA flows. Q602 behaves the same way when BUS- is above PE.
evidence: C2M1000170D.pdf p2: VSD 3.8 V (body diode). Netlist: Q601 D=IMDP_SW, S=PE; Q602 D=PE, S=IMDN_SW. The design note itself assumes 'pole above PE / pole below PE'. With G_a = 1/6.005 M on each pole and a battery pole conductance comparable to G_a, u = V(PE-BUS-) exceeds V_A whenever V_A is below roughly 0.4 x V_B.
proposed_fix: Use a back-to-back (common-source) SiC pair per switch, as the TPSI3050 two-wire application drives (SLVSFJ7D Fig 8-4/9-2), or put a >= 1600 V blocking diode in series with each test string.

finding: C_VDDP is drawn at 220 nF 25 V X7R 0603 nominal, which is the absolute minimum of the 220-330 nF range required in two-wire mode. Tolerance (+/-10 %) and DC-bias derating at the VDDP voltage put the real value below the minimum.
evidence: TPSI3050-Q1.pdf p5 (C_VDDP two-wire 220-330 nF, 'all capacitance values are absolute, derating should be applied'), sec. 9.3: 'the recommended absolute capacitance must be 220 nF, so if derating is required, a higher component value can be needed'.
proposed_fix: Use 270 nF (C0G, or X7R 0805/1206 50 V with bias derating checked) so the effective value stays within 220-330 nF.

finding: The AUX-HV input has no surge clamp, and its voltage design stops at 1100 V. It is fed from the port terminals behind the PV-PORT SPD (Ucpv 1000 V; Up <= 4 kV; the varistors barely conduct below ~1.2-1.5 kV). The input RC (30 ohm x 1.03 uF, tau 31 us) passes most of a differential transient to HV_BULK. Above ~1.36 kV on HV_BULK the switching MOSFET exceeds 1700 V (HV_BULK + VR 142 V + clamp >= 222 V); C101 is limited to 1.5 x 1300 V = 1950 V at most 10 times per life; the start-up cascode totals 3 x 600 V.
evidence: Calc: a 2.75 kV, 20 us differential residual on 1000 V raises HV_BULK by 1.75 kV x (1 - e^-20/31) -> 1.84 kV; a 2 kV, 50 us residual -> 1.80 kV; a slow 1.5 kV swell passes fully. C3M0900170J.pdf p1 VDS 1700 V; C4AQ.pdf p5 surge 1.5 x VNDC; BSS126.pdf p1 600 V each. sim/aux_hv_design.py sizes V_DS only up to VIN_TR = 1100 V; the port surge table (port report sec. 9) does not include AUX-HV.
proposed_fix: Add an input clamp on HV_BULK after the inrush resistors (TVS/MOV string clamping at <= ~1.25 kV, energy-rated for the surge current through 30 ohm), plus an input over-voltage lockout that stops switching above ~1150 V (so the switch sees HV_BULK only), coordinated with the port SPD.

location: AUX-HV sheet 01: F102 (Schurter 0090.1001, 1 A gPV) on the port-B (battery/bus) input PB_P; F101 on the PV port is adequate
finding: The input fuse's breaking capacity (20 kA at 1000 VDC, L/R < 2 ms) is below the port-B fault level the module design allows (20 kA assumed, <= 50 kA with L/R <= 1 ms). The 1 A link melts long before the upstream 160 A NH link (0.554 A2s vs ~19 kA2s), so it alone must interrupt the full prospective current for a short anywhere between the stud and the inrush resistors.
evidence: ASO-0090.1001.pdf p3-p4: breaking capacity 20 kA @ 1000 VDC, L/R < 2 ms; melting I2t 0.554 A2s. port_design report sec. 13: battery prospective short-circuit current <= 50 kA at the module terminals; A_IPSC_BATT 20 kA; report sec. 6.6: 160 A link melting 19 kA2s.
proposed_fix: Use a 1000-1500 VDC fuse with >= 50 kA DC breaking capacity at the required L/R for the port-B input, or put a fusible current-limiting resistor ahead of it, or cap the port-B prospective current at 20 kA in the requirements.

finding: A hard output short (or a load that holds Vout near 0) at an input above ~600 V drives the primary current in a staircase into core saturation. The minimum on-time (CS RC 150 ns plus tD 35-70 ns plus turn-off, 0.25-0.4 us at the 1 V limit) adds more current per cycle than the shorted secondary can reset, so the cycle-by-cycle limit cannot stop it. The current climbs past saturation until source degeneration and winding resistance limit it at roughly 6-8 A. That gives V_DS ~1485-1585 V at turn-off (87-93 % of 1700 V, above the design's 90 % transient rule), the CS node near its 6.3 V abs max, and about 50 W in the clamp. This persists for the 21 ms VDD hold-up of every hiccup cycle, or indefinitely if leakage-spike charging keeps VAUX up (report sec. 13 open item). The report's hiccup analysis does not cover it.
evidence: Calc (Lp 1.14 mH, fs 65.35 kHz, n 6, short-circuit reset 9 V on the primary): per cycle +0.22..0.35 A on vs -0.12 A off at 1000 V (+0.13..0.21 vs -0.12 at 600 V). CS reaches 1.0 V 330 ns after turn-on at I0 = 1.5 A. N97 Bsat 410 mT at 100 C is reached at ~2.3-2.5 A (310 mT at 1.74 A, aux_hv_spec b_lim_mT). V_DS = Vin + 2 x (123 + 10.5 x 8) x 1.075 + 40. SLUSEV2C p7: tD 35-70 ns, COMP-CS offset 1.15 V; p5 CS abs max 6.3 V; UCC28C5x has no frequency foldback or LEB.
proposed_fix: Add short-circuit protection that does not rely on VDD collapse: frequency foldback driven by the aux/VAUX level (e.g. a transistor that adds capacitance on RT/CT when VAUX is low, so t_off grows 5-10x), or a fast aux-undervoltage detector that pulls SS/COMP low after a few cycles; verify on a T1 sample at 1100 V with the output shorted.

location: AUX-HV sheet 03: current limit R312/R313 (0.75 ohm), clamp D308/D309 (SMBJ100A), D401, T301
finding: The supply has no time-limited overload protection. The cycle-by-cycle limit allows 34 W (min) / 58 W (typ) / 138 W (max) from a 30 W design and holds that level indefinitely while Vout stays above ~15 V. Already at the minimum limit (Ipk 1.19 A) the clamp TVS junctions reach ~155 C, and ~179 C at the typical limit (Tj max 150 C); the rectifier and T1 are similarly overstressed. Sustained overload is foreseeable: without the cabinet 24 V, the module's 24 V demand can exceed 30 W (contactor coils ~12 W plus fans, D-022), and the SYS eFuses (CTRL branch 4.5 A) do not bound it to 30 W.
evidence: Calc with the report's own model: clamp loss 1.56 W x (Ipk/0.932)^2 -> 2.54 W at 1.19 A, 3.18 W at 1.33 A, 5.44 W at 1.74 A; per SMBJ100A at 75 K/W (report sec. 9: 60 K/W board + 15 K/W junction-lead) -> Tj 155 / 179 / 264 C at 60 C ambient. aux_hv report sec. 6: limit delivers 34 / 58 / 138 W; SMBJ_Bourns.pdf Tj max 150 C.
proposed_fix: Add an overload timer (e.g. latch-off or hiccup when COMP sits at its clamp for > 50-100 ms, using the SS capacitor and a comparator or transistor), or size the clamp, rectifier and T1 for the current-limit power; state the 30 W load limit as a SYS-IO-AUX requirement.

location: AUX-HV sheet 03: Q301 (BC817-25) emitter VDD_E, D305 (BAT54), R305, D304
finding: During start-up and every hiccup, VDD (15-17 V) is present while VAUX ~ 0. The reverse leakage of the blocking Schottky D305 has no path except the reverse-biased base-emitter junction of Q301 (base held near 0 V through R305). VDD_E therefore climbs until the B-E junction breaks down, above the 5 V VEBO rating. Repeated reverse B-E avalanche degrades hFE, which the follower's VDD regulation depends on.
evidence: BC817.pdf p3: VEBO 5 V (V(BR)EBO min 5 V at 100 uA); BAT54.pdf p2: IR <= 2 uA at 25 V, 25 C, rising steeply with temperature (Fig. 2). Netlist: D305 A=VDD_E K=VDD; Q301 B=ZB, E=VDD_E, C=VAUX; R305 VAUX-ZB; D304 ZB-PGND.
proposed_fix: Add a resistor of ~100 k from VDD_E to PGND (or a diode across B-E) to sink the Schottky leakage.
